data.name: Sample - Fortinet FortiAIGate - 1.6.3
data.description: Sample playbooks for the "Fortinet FortiAIGate" connector. If you are planning to use the sample playbooks in your environment, ensure that you clone those playbooks and move them to a different collection, since the sample playbook collection gets deleted during connector upgrade and delete.

workflows.name: Renew Expiring FortiAIGate Keys in Vault
workflows.description:
Renews FortiAIGate virtual keys before they expire and puts each new secret into the HashiCorp Vault secret that holds it. FortiAIGate lists the keys that expire within Within (Days), and the ones already expired. Vault is then searched under Secret Folder for secrets whose custom metadata tag faig_key_id names one of those keys; Vault cannot search, so this lists the folder and reads each secret's metadata, never a secret value. A key with exactly one tagged secret is renewed by the child playbook "Renew FortiAIGate Key in Vault". A key no secret is tagged with is left to expire (no app uses it), and a key tagged on more than one secret is not touched and reported as a conflict, for a person.
Inputs: secret_folder (default lab), within_days (default 2) and extend_days (default 7; must be more than within_days, or every run would renew the same keys again). Outputs: expiring, renewed, failed, unused and conflicts. Run it from a schedule, for example every 15 minutes. The default HashiCorp Vault KV configuration needs read and list on the folder's metadata, patch on its metadata, and patch on its data - not read.

workflows.name: Renew FortiAIGate Key in Vault
workflows.description:
Renews one FortiAIGate virtual key and stores its new secret in the HashiCorp Vault secret that holds it. The key keeps its id, name, limits, policies and model access; its expiry moves to Extend By (Days) from now when it would come sooner. Only the api_key field of the secret is changed (an HTTP PATCH - other fields are kept), and the secret's metadata is stamped with faig_rotated_at and faig_expires_at. The new secret is then tested against the data plane.
If the renew is refused (a revoked key, say), outcome is renew_failed and nothing changes. If the Vault write fails, the run says so and stores the secret nowhere: the old secret is already dead, so fix Vault and run this again - a rotate can be repeated. Called by "Renew Expiring FortiAIGate Keys in Vault"; inputs key_id, secret_path, extend_days. Outputs: key_id, key_name, secret_path, outcome (renewed, renew_failed or write_failed), method, expires_at, verified.

groups.name: Note: RenewKey
groups.description: Errors are caught so the child always ends on a result (a revoked key, say), and one bad key cannot stop the parent's loop.

groups.name: Note: WriteSecret
groups.description: Changes only api_key. Retried on network and server errors.

workflows.name: Onboard FortiAIGate Key to Vault
workflows.description:
API endpoint that creates a FortiAIGate virtual key for an app and stores it in a NEW HashiCorp Vault secret, tagged so the renewal playbooks can find it. POST a JSON body: secret_path (required), key_name (default: the secret path), workspace (name or id), providers (default openai), expires_in_days (default 7) and fields (an object of extra secret fields, for example base_url and model).
The secret path must be free: the run checks first and writes with check-and-set 0, so an existing secret is never overwritten. If the Vault write fails, the new key is revoked, so no working key is left outside Vault. The secret's metadata gets faig_key_id, faig_key_name, faig_expires_at and faig_created_at. Ends with key_name, secret_path, key_id, expires_at and outcome (created, path_in_use or write_failed). The default HashiCorp Vault KV configuration needs create on the data path and read and patch on the metadata path.
